None of these establishes perceptual quality.",

accepted_claims: Receipt facts: project titan_audio_ecosystem; direct_reference_input false; prompt_is_post_render_output true; waveform_filter_tests_latent_diffusion false; canonical_mutation_allowed false (research/audio_context.md:76-83).
Forward has no text prompt, target audio, prime, or external reference argument (research/audio_context.md:13-15; src/main.rs:5108-5122).

Target sampling occurs after forward; the current target cannot change the same precomputed chunk (research/audio_context.md:16-18; src/main.rs:7041-7107; docs/AUDIO_SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENTATION_PLAN.md:101).
The prompt file is written after rendering and prime extraction (research/audio_context.md:19-21; src/main.rs:8682-8697).
Offline waveform filtering tests signal processing only; it is not a proxy for latent-field diffusion, and a trained diffusion/flow decoder is also not a proxy (research/audio_context.md:64-67).
Canonical checkpoints, corpus, existing WAVs, and the normal renderer/training must remain intact; offline tests may create copied WAVs and sidecar receipts (research/audio_context.md:68-70).
The 60 s prime is selected by a score with no width or harshness term and can amplify a within-run outlier (research/audio_context.md:51-53; src/main.rs:8141-8145, 8463-8481).
The full 600 s render is not uniformly centered; per-minute correlation ranges 0.740-0.992 (deepseek_packet.md:31-35).

The audible path ends in loss-visible tanh, a stateful DC blocker, and whole-file peak normalization; a sub-0 dBFS sample peak does not exclude nonlinear saturation or perceptual harshness (research/audio_context.md:48-50; src/main.rs:8059-8076, 8451-8455).

Side derives from L-R before a delayed scaled side stage; learned width is bounded 0.05..0.50; global pan is +/-0.10; increasing side gain cannot synthesize missing side information (research/audio_context.md:44-47; src/main.rs:5565-5603; src/stereo.rs:3-11, 28-41).
Pan-center loss penalizes the bounded audible residual pan and does not directly reward correlation=1 (research/audio_context.md:44-47; src/stereo.rs:21-26).
The low-band loss term measures the first log band; it is not the whole 20-200 Hz measurement (research/audio_context.md:40-43; METRICS.md:64-65).
ultrasonic_ratio is a pre-master aliasing/foldback guardrail, not a harshness score (deepseek_packet.md:40-41; METRICS.md:94-95).

AdamW moments are persisted and resumed under strict compatibility conditions; the real reproducibility limitation is checkpoint-set transactionality (docs/AUDIO_SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENTATION_PLAN.md:112-124).
The three latest WAVs form one sequential continuation lineage, not independent seeds or matched arms (research/audio_context.md:28-29).

Do not fork training, do not modify the renderer, do not change prime selection, and do not introduce any diffusion mechanism. conclusions: The six advisory reviews agree on the mandatory receipt facts and on the core causal ordering: forward has no reference/target/prompt argument, target sampling occurs after forward, the prompt file is written after rendering, offline waveform filtering is not a latent-diffusion proxy, and canonical artifacts must remain intact. This agreement is advisory, not evidence; it is corroborated by the cited source lines.

The reviews disagree substantively on the locus of the reported center bias and harshness. The disagreement is real and is not resolved by the supplied evidence: the prime is a selected within-run outlier, the three WAVs are a sequential lineage, and no blinded listening exists.

The strongest supported claim is that the 60 s prime is a within-run outlier: the full 600 s render has per-minute L/R correlation 0.740-0.992, and the prime is drawn from a 0.990-0.992 interval (deepseek_packet.md:31-35). Prime selection uses field entropy, activity health, structured complexity, and stagnation, with no width or harshness term (src/main.rs:8141-8145, 8463-8481).

The second supported claim is that the audible path ends in loss-visible tanh, a stateful DC blocker, and whole-file peak normalization to -1 dBFS (src/main.rs:8059-8076, 8451-8455), so a sub-0 dBFS sample peak does not exclude nonlinear saturation or perceptual harshness (research/audio_context.md:48-50).

The third supported claim is that the renderer cannot synthesize missing side information: side derives from L-R, is scaled by a bounded learned width (0.05..0.50) and a bounded side gain, and is delayed by a 16-sample Haas history before recombination (src/main.rs:5565-5603; src/stereo.rs:3-11, 28-41).

The reviews' proposed experiments are largely redundant and mostly offline. The cheapest discriminating set is: (a) per-interval absolute L+R band power and stereo geometry on the existing full WAV; (b) prime re-selection under an alternative width/harshness-aware score; (c) post-path ablation on copied WAVs; (d) frozen first-chunk invariance negative control. None of these establishes perceptual quality.

No review establishes that the harshness is caused by the learned renderer, the post path, the target mix, or the prime selection. All such attributions remain hypotheses. The listener report is a single uncontrolled observation (research/audio_context.md:58-60).

The 'diffusion' framing is a category error for this codebase: no latent-diffusion module exists (research/audio_context.md:62-63), and neither waveform filtering nor a trained diffusion/flow decoder is a proxy for latent-field diffusion (research/audio_context.md:64-67).

Compare the prime interval against the full-run distribution. This separates prime-selection outlier effects from run-wide harshness and center bias without touching canonical files.

context_receipt.summary: Titan Audio v9 is a CPU Rust NCA/GRU/DDSP ecosystem. Forward takes world state and host controls, not text or target audio. Target audio is sampled after forward and affects loss, optimizer, and later host ecology. The prompt file is written after rendering. Offline waveform filtering tests signal processing, not latent-field diffusion. Canonical checkpoints, corpus, and existing WAVs must remain intact. The listener's harsh/centered report is consistent with measured correlation 0.991, side/mid -23.31 dB, and 2-6 kHz fraction 47.3% in the latest tagged prime, but no blinded listening has been done and the prime is a within-run outlier.

disagreements.claim_a: CLAIM A: The center bias is primarily a prime-selection artifact. The full 600 s run is not uniformly centered (per-minute corr 0.740-0.992), and the 60 s prime was selected from a 0.990-0.992 interval by a score that ignores width and harshness.
disagreements.claim_b: CLAIM B: The center bias is primarily a learned-renderer drift. The width head, side control, pan head, and Haas side path have moved toward mono, and the prime merely samples that state.
disagreements.discriminating_experiment: Per-interval audit of the existing full 600 s WAV: compute non-overlapping 60 s L/R correlation, side/mid, balance, and absolute L+R band power in 20-200 Hz, 2-6 kHz, 6-20 kHz, and total. Compare the selected prime interval against the full-run distribution. If the prime is an extreme outlier in correlation and side/mid, A is supported. If most windows are similarly center-heavy, B is supported. This is offline, uses copied WAVs, and does not touch canonical files.
disagreements.why_they_differ: They differ on locus: A attributes the observed center bias to the selection window (a measurement/selection artifact), B attributes it to the learned renderer state (a model property). Both are consistent with the same WAV because the prime is a 60 s window chosen by a score that ignores width, while the full run is heterogeneous and the trace shows drifted width/pan values. The supplied evidence contains both a heterogeneous full run and a drifted width/pan trace, so neither claim is excluded.

disagreements.claim_a: CLAIM A: The harshness is primarily post-render nonlinearity (tanh at 0.92, DC blocker, peak normalization to -1 dBFS) rather than the learned renderer's spectral content.
disagreements.claim_b: CLAIM B: The harshness is primarily the learned renderer's spectral content (scan partials, wavefolder, FM, upper-mid emphasis), with the post path as a secondary contributor.
disagreements.discriminating_experiment: Post-path ablation on copied WAVs: produce level-matched variants with (a) tanh bypassed, (b) DC blocker bypassed, (c) both bypassed and re-normalized to the same -1 dBFS, and (d) identity. Measure absolute L+R band power in 2-6 kHz and 6-20 kHz and an intermodulation proxy. If bypassing the post path materially reduces high-band energy, A is supported; if not, B is supported. This is signal-domain only and is not a latent-diffusion proxy.
disagreements.why_they_differ: They differ on stage: A locates harshness in the fixed post path, B locates it in the learned renderer before the post path. Both can contribute because the post path is applied after the differentiable renderer and the supplied WAVs are post-master. The supplied metrics do not separate the two stages.

disagreements.claim_a: CLAIM A: The learned drift toward mono is intrinsic to the renderer/optimizer trajectory (width head near its low rail, pan at its +0.10 limit).
disagreements.claim_b: CLAIM B: The learned drift is target-driven via the stereo/correlation losses (STEREO_SIDE_LOSS_WEIGHT 0.30, STEREO_CORRELATION_LOSS_WEIGHT 0.95, STEREO_LEVEL_LOSS_WEIGHT 0.45) and the target episode in force.
disagreements.discriminating_experiment: Read-only target attribution: from the trace's target_file/target_frame/target_chunks_left fields, identify the target episode in force during the prime interval and report its correlation and 2-6 kHz fraction. If the target is itself center-heavy and bright, B is supported. If the target is not, A is supported. This does not change the forward pass and does not call the mutating manifest path.
disagreements.why_they_differ: They differ on cause of the learned drift. The forward pass has no target argument, but target losses affect weights and later host feedback; the current chunk cannot be changed by the current target, but later chunks can. The supplied evidence does not identify which target episode was in force during the prime interval, and the trace is a sampled summary.

disagreements.claim_a: CLAIM A: The center bias and harshness are separable from the supplied evidence by offline tests on the existing WAVs.
disagreements.claim_b: CLAIM B: The center bias and harshness are not separable from the supplied evidence because the prime is a within-run outlier and the three WAVs are a sequential lineage, not matched arms.
disagreements.discriminating_experiment: Run the per-interval audit and the post-path ablation on copied WAVs. If the per-interval audit shows the prime is an extreme outlier and the post-path ablation shows a material high-band change, A is supported for those two questions. If neither reaches a pre-registered threshold, B is supported and a matched-arm or independent-seed experiment is required. Pre-register thresholds before running.
disagreements.why_they_differ: They differ on whether the existing artifacts are sufficient. A treats the full 600 s WAV as a distribution that can be audited per interval; B treats the confounds (elapsed training, target mix, world state, prime selection) as too entangled for attribution. Both are consistent with the supplied evidence.

proposed_experiments.controls: Identical windowing and FFT parameters across files; report absolute power, not only fractions; do not modify originals; record SHA256 of every copied file and sidecar receipt.
proposed_experiments.cost: Low; offline, no training, no model load.
proposed_experiments.expected_discriminator: If the prime interval is an extreme outlier in correlation and side/mid relative to the full run, center bias is partly a selection artifact. If 2-6 kHz absolute power is elevated across the full run, harshness is not only a prime-selection artifact.
proposed_experiments.limits: Signal-domain measurement only; does not establish perceptual harshness.
proposed_experiments.method: Copy the latest full 600 s WAV and the untagged parent WAV to a sidecar directory. Compute non-overlapping 60 s interval statistics: L/R Pearson correlation, side/mid dB, L/R balance dB, absolute L+R band power in 20-200 Hz, 200-2000 Hz, 2-6 kHz, 6-20 kHz, and total, plus integrated loudness. Compare the selected prime interval against the full-run distribution.
proposed_experiments.name: E1: Per-interval absolute band-power and stereo-geometry audit
proposed_experiments.purpose: Separate prime-selection artifact from run-wide center bias and harshness, and replace fraction-only mid-channel estimates with absolute L+R band power.

proposed_experiments.controls: Use the same window length and estimator; do not change the selection in the canonical run; report both selected windows and their metrics.
proposed_experiments.expected_discriminator: If the current-selection window is a statistical outlier on correlation and 2-6 kHz relative to the alternative objectives, the selection-objective story is supported.
proposed_experiments.limits: Does not change the renderer or checkpoint; does not establish perceptual quality.
proposed_experiments.method: Recompute the chunk_scores sliding window over the full render using the same formula as src/main.rs:8141-8145, and separately using an alternative score that includes a side/mid term and a 2-6 kHz balance term. Compare the selected intervals' correlation, side/mid, and 2-6 kHz fraction.
proposed_experiments.name: E2: Prime re-selection sensitivity audit
proposed_experiments.purpose: Test whether the current prime-selection score systematically prefers center-heavy or bright intervals.

proposed_experiments.controls: Level-match all variants to the same integrated loudness; use paired intervals; do not modify originals; record applied gains in sidecar receipts.
proposed_experiments.expected_discriminator: If bypassing the post path materially reduces high-band energy, the post path is a contributor. If not, the harshness originates earlier in the renderer.
proposed_experiments.limits: Signal-domain only; not a proxy for latent-field diffusion; does not establish perceptual harshness.
proposed_experiments.method: On copied WAVs, produce level-matched variants: (a) identity, (b) tanh bypassed, (c) DC blocker bypassed, (d) both bypassed and re-normalized to the same -1 dBFS. Measure absolute L+R band power in 2-6 kHz and 6-20 kHz, crest factor, and an intermodulation proxy.
proposed_experiments.name: E3: Post-path ablation on copied WAVs
proposed_experiments.purpose: Separate tanh saturation, DC blocker, and peak normalization contributions to measured high-band energy.

proposed_experiments.controls: Hold all world state, phases, controls, RNG, model, and optimizer identical; vary only the target chunk.
proposed_experiments.cost: Low to moderate; requires harness access, no training.
proposed_experiments.expected_discriminator: Identical current-chunk audio supports the no-reference-input claim. Any difference would contradict the documented causal order and require source re-audit.
proposed_experiments.limits: Tests the current chunk only; later host feedback may still differ.
proposed_experiments.method: Clone identical pre-forward state, run model.forward with two different target chunks presented to the loss, and compare the emitted current-chunk waveform byte-for-byte. Repeat across several steps.
proposed_experiments.name: E4: Frozen first-chunk invariance negative control
proposed_experiments.purpose: Confirm that target audio does not condition the current chunk's forward pass.

proposed_experiments.controls: Randomized order, hidden labels, level matching to integrated LUFS, documented exclusion rules, null trials.
proposed_experiments.cost: Requires listeners and a protocol not currently available.
proposed_experiments.expected_discriminator: Consistent ratings above chance support the perceptual claim; chance-level ratings do not.
proposed_experiments.limits: Does not by itself attribute the percept to a specific mechanism.
proposed_experiments.method: Present level-matched, order-randomized, label-hidden excerpts (prime, non-prime interval, post-path-bypassed variant, mono-collapse control) to multiple listeners with a fixed rating instrument covering harshness and center bias. Report inter-rater agreement and false-positive rate from null trials.
proposed_experiments.name: E5: Blinded, level-matched listening protocol
proposed_experiments.purpose: Establish or refute the perceptual claim.

Rejected: that waveform-domain filtering or a trained diffusion/flow decoder is a proxy for latent-field diffusion (research/audio_context.md:64-67).
Rejected: that the whole 600 s WAV is uniformly centered. The packet reports per-minute correlation 0.740-0.992 (deepseek_packet.md:31-35).

Rejected: that the supplied MID-channel spectral fractions establish absolute bass loss or absolute high-band harshness. They are fraction-normalized mid-channel estimates (research/audio_context.md:54-57; deepseek_packet.md:19-22).
Rejected: that ultrasonic_ratio establishes or excludes perceptual harshness (deepseek_packet.md:40-41; METRICS.md:94-95).
Rejected: that the listener report establishes perceptual improvement or degradation. No blinded listening has been performed (research/audio_context.md:58-60).
Rejected: that the current target audio conditions the current chunk's forward pass (research/audio_context.md:16-18; docs/AUDIO_SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENTATION_PLAN.md:101).
Rejected: that a zero-output identity branch proves anything beyond bypass behavior (research/audio_context.md:66-67).
Rejected: that the three WAVs are independent seeds or matched arms (research/audio_context.md:28-29).
Rejected: that the provisional caveat that AdamW state may not be persisted is correct for current Audio v9 (docs/AUDIO_SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENTATION_PLAN.md:112-124).
uncertainties: No controlled blinded listening has been performed; perceptual harshness and center bias are listener-reported, not measured (research/audio_context.md:58-60).

The supplied spectral fractions are MID-channel sampled FFT power fractions; they can change with denominator or stereo changes and are not absolute L+R band power. Bass 'loss' is not established without absolute and total L+R band power (research/audio_context.md:54-57).

The three latest WAVs are one sequential continuation lineage, not independent seeds or matched arms; cross-WAV comparisons confound elapsed training, target mix, world state, and optimizer state (research/audio_context.md:28-29, 37-39).

The training trace is a sampled summary (704 rows, steps 74,340-81,370); it does not identify which target episode was in force during the selected prime interval, and the underlying trace file was not supplied for independent recomputation.

Pre-side-scale renderer taps and frequency-specific loss gradients are missing, so the contribution of the learned width head vs the Haas side path vs the mid/side stage vs the target-driven loss cannot be separated from the supplied WAVs alone (research/audio_context.md:71-74).
The exact contribution of the wavefolder, scan synthesis, excitation noise, and tanh saturation to perceived harshness is not measured.

The checkpoint-set transactionality caveat (model -> optimizer -> world publish order) means the latest run may not be mathematically bit-exact with its recorded step; this is a reproducibility limitation, not a sound-quality claim (docs/AUDIO_SCIENTIFIC_INSTRUMENTATION_PLAN.md:112-124).
Whether the two quarantine-provenance manifest entries entered gradients is unknown from manifest roles alone (research/audio_context.md:33-36).
Downstream priming outcomes are missing; any effect of the prompt on an external system is outside this experiment (research/audio_context.md:19-21, 71-74).
The reviews' proposed experiments are untested proposals; none has been executed in this review.
